summary: When the hero is trapped in an unjoined pit and fires a horizontal wand of digging into a diggable adjacent room, C creates the adjacent pit before setting reciprocal conjoined-pit bits. The JavaScript zap_dig caller skipped the existing dighole implementation, leaving the target cell as floor and shifting later movement behavior.

source.branch: zap_dig sees pitdig with a TT_PIT under the hero, a valid horizontal direction, no already-conjoined adjacent pit, and adj_pit_checks permits the adjacent ordinary room; the selected recording exercises this through a WAN_DIGGING ray.
callers: zap.c:weffects dispatches WAN_DIGGING to zap_dig; dozap is the wand command entry.
dependencies: dighole(TRUE, TRUE, &cc) has its result discarded here; JS dig.js:dighole already implements the pit-only magical path and must be invoked for its effects.
adj_pit_checks supplies the mutable-coordinate permission/message check before the call.

evidence: Saved queue entry challenges/manifests/v55.json case v55-conjoined-pit-horizontal-dig-action3 (manifest digest 3c17045e325445fd449f429e13ff79d2eb858dc308a82f9e2a7c371ad9c56105; recording digest 0b36f331858554a6c0d84df605a027f4621fce06e97b42af01ea133f843a1ae5; evaluation challenges/evaluations/baseline-261c3097d-v55.json at 261c3097de5e63e488e143c622a3fa8157b750eb): first screen difference is step 195, when C displays the adjacent pit and JS still has floor; the baseline later differs by one RNG call at step 248.

nethack-c/upstream/src/dig.c:1600-1657 shows zap_dig setting pitdig from u.utraptype == TT_PIT, checking the adjacent location, calling dighole(TRUE, TRUE, &cc) at 1649, re-reading t_at(), then setting reciprocal conjoined bits and flow coordinates.

js/zap.js:6083-6140 has the corresponding horizontal pit branch. On an allowed adjacent location it currently calls note_unported("dig.c dighole") and immediately re-reads t_at(), so no pit exists to link.

nethack-c/upstream/src/dig.c:885-1022 defines dighole; the ordinary room/pit-only arm reaches digactualhole(..., PIT), updates the tile/trap, and runs spot_checks. js/dig.js:dighole implements that arm; zap_dig discards the C return, so invoking the existing owner is sufficient without expanding the task into the helper.
